Fit semantic topics to documents

Source: R/topics.R
topics.Rd

topics() fits an embedding-based topic model: it groups texts, or the sentences, clauses, or phrases of texts, by what they mean rather than by the words they share, and each group is a topic. Each unit is represented by a Sentence-BERT embedding (Reimers and Gurevych 2019), a vector in which texts of similar meaning lie close together, and the embeddings are partitioned into groups of semantically similar texts.

Every unit is assigned to one of n_topics topics by k-means clustering (Lloyd 1982) of the L2-normalized embeddings, started from farthest-point initial centers. The fit is deterministic: the same input always gives the same topics, and no random seed is involved. Each topic is described by its distinctive terms, scored by class-based TF-IDF (Grootendorst 2022; Mendonca and Figueira 2025), and by its representative units, those nearest its center. By default a topic is labeled by its most central text. Topics are numbered by size, largest first, unless seeds fix their order. Unlike latent Dirichlet allocation, the model does not represent a text as a mixture of word distributions, so it does not depend on words co-occurring within texts, which they rarely do in short texts.

The result, an object of class sbert_topic_model, shows which kinds of content a corpus holds and how much of the corpus each kind accounts for.

To choose the number of topics and the unit of analysis, compare candidate fits with compare_topics(). To fit several models to one corpus, prepare it once with topic_corpus(). New texts are assigned to the fitted topics by predict(), and each document's mixture of topics is given by topic_gamma(). To merge the topics of an existing fit, use reduce_topics().

Usage

topics(
  text,
  n_topics,
  column = NULL,
  model = NULL,
  embeddings = NULL,
  batch_size = 32L,
  iter_max = 100L,
  n_terms = 10L,
  n_representatives = 5L,
  stop_words = default_stop_words(),
  min_term_frequency = 1L,
  min_token_length = 2L,
  weighting = c("ctfidf", "bm25"),
  reduce_frequent_words = FALSE,
  stem = FALSE,
  keep_embeddings = TRUE,
  seeds = NULL,
  seed_embeddings = NULL,
  fixed_seeds = FALSE,
  cores = 1L,
  numbers = c("keep", "remove"),
  roman_numerals = c("keep", "remove"),
  section_numbers = c("keep", "remove"),
  segment = c("document", "sentence", "clause", "phrase"),
  max_tokens = NULL,
  merge_below = 0L,
  min_content = 0,
  label = c("representative", "terms")
)

Arguments

text

Documents: a character vector with one document per element, a data frame together with column, or a corpus prepared by topic_corpus().

n_topics

Number of topics: an integer of at least 2 and at most the number of modeled units.

column

Name of the text column when text is a data frame. The other columns are carried into the document table. Rows whose text is missing, blank, or the placeholder "[No abstract available]" are dropped, and so are their rows of embeddings. NULL (default) for a character vector.

model

The encoder: a model from load_model(), a pinned model name from models(), or NULL (default) for the default model. Not used when embeddings are given.

embeddings

Optional numeric matrix of precomputed embeddings, one row per modeled unit (per document, or per segment with segment). When it is given, no model is loaded. Default NULL.

batch_size

Texts encoded per model call (default 32).

iter_max

Maximum number of k-means iterations (default 100).

n_terms

Terms stored per topic (default 10).

n_representatives

Representative units stored per topic (default 5).

stop_words

Words excluded from the topic terms; default stop_words(). character() turns the filter off.

min_term_frequency

Minimum corpus-wide frequency of a term (default 1).

min_token_length

Minimum length of a term, in characters (default 2).

weighting

Term weighting: "ctfidf" (default) or "bm25", which down-weights terms shared by many topics more strongly.

reduce_frequent_words

Whether to take the square root of within-topic term frequencies before weighting (default FALSE).

stem

Whether to merge inflected forms of a term under one Porter stem, shown as its most frequent form (default FALSE; needs the SnowballC package).

keep_embeddings

Whether to store the normalized embeddings in the model (default TRUE). Without them, reduce_topics(), topic_membership(), and representatives() need the embeddings supplied again.

seeds

Optional guided topics: a character vector, or a list of character vectors, of seed words or descriptions, one element per seeded topic. The embedding of seed i is the starting center of topic i, and the names of seeds, if any, become topic labels. Default NULL.

seed_embeddings

Matrix of seed embeddings, one row per seed. Needed when seeds are combined with precomputed embeddings.

fixed_seeds

If TRUE, the seed centers are held fixed and each unit joins its nearest seed (zero-shot classification); n_topics must equal the number of seeds, and a topic may be empty. Default FALSE.

cores

Number of forked worker processes for tokenization (default 1; Unix-alikes only). Results do not depend on it.

numbers, roman_numerals, section_numbers

Whether to "keep" (default) or "remove" digit-only tokens, Roman-numeral tokens, and section or list numbering (1.2.3, 1.) from the topic terms. They change the terms only, not the text that is embedded; to clean the text, use clean_corpus().

segment

Unit of analysis: "document" (default), or "sentence", "clause", or "phrase", which split each document with segment() and fit the topics to the segments, so that a document can take part in several topics.

max_tokens, merge_below, min_content

Segmentation options passed to segment(), for segmented fits only: the maximum segment length (in the model's tokens, or in words with precomputed embeddings; default NULL, no limit), the number of words below which a segment is joined to its neighbor (default 0), and the minimum share of letters for a segment to be kept (default 0; see content_ratio()).

label

How topics are labeled: "representative" (default), the most central text shortened to 60 characters, or "terms", the three most distinctive terms. Named seeds override both.

Value

An object of class sbert_topic_model, a list with

documents

One row per modeled unit (document, or segment): document_id, document_name, segment (segmented fits only), text, topic, label, and distance (cosine distance to the topic center), followed by the columns carried from a data frame.

topics

One row per topic: topic, label, n_documents, proportion, and withinss.

terms, representatives

The stored terms and representative units of each topic.

centers

Numeric matrix of topic centers, one row per topic: the k-means means of the L2-normalized embeddings. They are not rescaled, so their norms are below one; verbs that use cosine similarity normalize them first.

embeddings

The normalized embeddings, or NULL when keep_embeddings = FALSE.

diagnostics

Sums of squares (totss, tot_withinss, betweenss), iterations, converged (whether k-means converged within iter_max), warnings (warnings raised by stats::kmeans()), and algorithm.

model, settings

The identity of the embedding model and the settings of the fit, which later verbs reuse.

Read it through its accessors rather than its fields: as.data.frame() with what = "documents", "topics", "terms", or "representatives"; topic_sizes(); terms(); representatives(); and summary(), which also reports a fit that did not converge.

Conditions

Errors of class sbert_bad_input for conflicting arguments, embeddings without one row per unit, more topics than distinct embeddings, or a model, embeddings, or different segment combined with a prepared corpus; sbert_missing_package for stem = TRUE without SnowballC; sbert_no_terms when no term passes the filters; and sbert_clustering_failed when k-means fails or leaves a topic empty. Arguments of the wrong type or range fail a plain stopifnot() check. When a model is used, the errors of load_model() and encode() apply. A warning of class sbert_no_converge when k-means reaches iter_max without converging; the fit is still returned. Errors inherit sbert_error and warnings sbert_warning.

References

Reimers, N. and Gurevych, I. (2019). Sentence-BERT: Sentence embeddings using Siamese BERT-networks. Proceedings of EMNLP-IJCNLP 2019, 3982–3992. doi:10.18653/v1/D19-1410

Grootendorst, M. (2022). BERTopic: Neural topic modeling with a class-based TF-IDF procedure. arXiv:2203.05794.

Mendonca, M. and Figueira, A. (2025). Modeling political discourse with Sentence-BERT and BERTopic. arXiv:2510.22904.

Lloyd, S. P. (1982). Least squares quantization in PCM. IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, 28(2), 129–137. doi:10.1109/TIT.1982.1056489

See also

compare_topics() to choose the number of topics; topic_corpus() to prepare a corpus once; name_topics() to name the topics; plot() for figures; predict() and topic_gamma() for new texts and topic mixtures; feedback_embeddings for the example data.

Examples

# 600 distinct feedback messages with their precomputed embeddings
corpus <- head(dedupe(feedback_translations, column = "translation"), 600)
topic_model <- topics(corpus, n_topics = 6, column = "translation",
                      embeddings = feedback_embeddings)
topic_model
#> <sbert_topic_model>
#>   documents: 600 
#>   topics: 6
#>   model: precomputed embeddings
#>   algorithm: deterministic k-means (Lloyd)
#>   topic sizes: 223, 133, 131, 49, 37, 27
#>   between/total SS: 22.6%
topic_sizes(topic_model, weights = "n")
#>   topic                                                       label n_documents

#> 4     4 Are you sure you have fewer pictures in the red box than...          49

# Sentence-level fit: one embedding per sentence
documents <- c(
  "Cats chase mice. Stocks and bonds trade.",
  "Dogs chase balls. Markets price shares."
)
sentence_model <- topics(
  documents, n_topics = 2, segment = "sentence",
  embeddings = rbind(c(1, 0), c(0, 1), c(0.9, 0.1), c(0.1, 0.9))
)
topic_sizes(sentence_model, by = "document")
#>   topic                   label n_documents proportion
#> 1     1        Cats chase mice.           2          1
#> 2     2 Stocks and bonds trade.           2          1
topic_gamma(sentence_model)
#>   document_id topic gamma n_segments
#> 1           1     1   0.5          2
#> 2           1     2   0.5          2
#> 3           2     1   0.5          2
#> 4           2     2   0.5          2
